title: RWB-P6-E4038-APP: no dispute operation, dispute table, deviation operation or customer principal is specified for rwb-comms
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.17; TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1, T5.2, T6.1 and appendix T-A.1; legacy RWB-E4-038
section: 12.1 REST operations provided; 11 Data; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 10 Authority
description: FEAT-COM-04 asks that the customer raise a dispute, which opens X1 and applies the contact stop, and no source gives the elements that would carry it in the target. TSD P6 appendix T-A.1 lists eleven operations and none of them raises a dispute, and TSD P6 T3.1 has notice, template, merge_field and signature_request and no dispute table, so the two operations, the DisputeRequest and DisputeAnswer shapes and the dispute_intake table are fixed by RWB-P6-E4038-CON and their field types are left to the baseline review. No source publishes a deviation operation of rwb-deviation that opens X1 for a customer dispute, so the open and the read are declared as consumed with the placeholder and a fake derived from R-DEV-01, R-DEV-02 and R-UNI-04. TSD P6 T6.1 has no customer row, so the principal of the action is the authenticated customer of LINE OA or HOME.SCB behind gateway-bff and not a Workbench role. The legacy permission, screen and endpoint rows of this key (Litigation C and R, SCR-33, POST /cases/{caseId}/notices and GET /notices/{noticeId}) describe the notice and template features and are not the rows of this feature, which is a conflict between the legacy story body and its own tables.
evidence: FSD P6 A2.17.1 and A2.17.2 name the outcome and the channels LINE OA and HOME.SCB only; TSD P6 T-A.1 has API-P6-001 to API-P6-011 with no dispute operation; TSD P6 T3.1 lists no dispute entity; TSD P6 T6.1 lists staff and partner roles only; legacy RWB-E4-038 Endpoints, Permission checks and Screen and states name Litigation rights, SCR-33 and the notice endpoints.
area: rwb-comms contract and data; rwb-deviation contract; customer channel authorisation
owner_role: Tech lead, with the rwb-deviation owner and the platform route owner
proposed: Fix the two operations, the shapes and the dispute_intake table in RWB-P6-E4038-CON, consume the deviation open and read on a fake with the placeholder, and treat the customer principal as gateway-bff's; carry the legacy rows as the notice and template features' and confirm the field list, the deviation operation and the customer authorisation in the baseline review.

title: RWB-P6-E4038-CON: the dispute contract baseline rests on an unspecified operation, table and deviation row, and the legacy rows of the key are a conflict
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 appendix T-A.1, T3.1 and T6.1; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.17; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-04, R-DEV-01, R-DEV-02
section: 12.1 REST operations provided; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 11 Data; 8 Business rules BR14
description: The contract baseline declares two operations and one table that no source names, so their paths, shapes, field types and state vocabulary are this baseline's own decision and are marked as such throughout. The deviation open and the deviation read are consumed without a published path, request or answer, and X1's code, owner and service level are taken from R-DEV-01, R-DEV-02 and R-UNI-04 only. The customer is the principal of both operations and no role row of TSD P6 T6.1 describes a customer, so the session, the scope and the coarse permission are declared as gateway-bff's. The legacy rows around the two criteria (SCR-33 Template approval, Litigation C and Litigation R, and the two notice endpoints) belong to the notice and template features and are named as that feature's rather than copied into a criterion, which is a conflict between the legacy story body and its tables.
evidence: TSD P6 T-A.1 ends at API-P6-011 with no dispute operation; TSD P6 T3.1 has four entities and no dispute entity; TSD P6 T6.1 has no customer row; no Ownership Map row names a deviation open or a dispute operation; legacy RWB-E4-038 Screen and states names SCR-33 and its Permission checks name Litigation rights.
area: rwb-comms contract; rwb-deviation contract; gateway-bff route
owner_role: Tech lead, with the solution architect for the Ownership Map rows
proposed: Baseline the two operations, the shapes and the dispute_intake table as declared here, ask the rwb-deviation owner to publish the deviation open and read, and let gateway-bff declare the customer session and scope; confirm each value at the consumer sign-off.
